origins: Some grew up hearing that real strength means toughing things out. Taking medicine for pain, blood pressure, diabetes, depression, or anxiety can then feel like failure of will. Shame keeps some from starting or from being honest with their doctor.
teaches: Jesus said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick.” Paul told Timothy to “use a little wine instead, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments” (1 Timothy 5:23). Luke, “the beloved physician,” traveled with Paul (Colossians 4:14). The good Samaritan treated wounds with oil and wine. God often uses doctors and medicines as His means of care. Strength is not refusing help. Wisdom is using the gifts God provides.
self_statements: Strong people do not need pills.
I should be able to handle this myself.
errors: Believing I am either strong and drug-free or weak.
Predicting that I will depend on it forever.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that I am weak.
questions: Where did I learn that needing medicine is weak?
Would I say the same to someone with a heart condition or diabetes?
What would my life be like without this treatment?
What does Scripture say about doctors and remedies?
What do I fear about taking it?
What questions should I ask my doctor?
truth: Medicine is one of God’s ways of caring for His people. Using it wisely, with my doctor’s guidance, is not weakness. It is stewardship of the body God gave me.
hw_truths: I can ask my doctor questions.
log: Each week, note one way you followed through on care.
actions: List what worries you about medication.
Bring questions to the next visit.
Do not stop suddenly without medical advice.
Remember the sick need a doctor.
prayer: Lord, thank You for doctors and medicine. Free me from shame, and help me use these gifts wisely and faithfully. Amen.
